q: Homeostasis is the ability of an organism to maintain a relatively constant _____ environment, even when the external environment is changing.
e: Homeostasis is the ability of an organism to maintain a relatively constant internal environment, even when the external environment is changing. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits. The environment is everything around an organism, biotic and abiotic. Physical is different: biophysics uses physical laws; it is not the same as biochemistry.

q: In plants, extra water is removed by transpiration and _____.
e: In plants, extra water is removed by transpiration and guttation. Guttation pushes liquid water out of hydathodes when root pressure is high. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata. Photosynthesis is different: photosynthesis builds glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using chlorophyll and light.

q: About 85-90% of water lost from a plant is lost by _____ transpiration.
e: About 85-90% of water lost from a plant is lost by stomatal transpiration. Transpiration is the evaporation of water from leaves, mainly through stomata. Cuticular is not stomatal.

q: Guttation is the expelling of excess water or nutrients through tiny openings called _____ on the tips or edges of leaves.
e: Guttation is the expelling of excess water or nutrients through tiny openings called hydathodes on the tips or edges of leaves. Guttation pushes liquid water out of hydathodes when root pressure is high. Stomata is different: stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out.

q: Padonmar kya ($Nelumbo$ $nucifera$) has _____ activities to maintain relatively stable tissue temperatures.
e: Padonmar kya (Nelumbo nucifera) has thermoregulation activities to maintain relatively stable tissue temperatures. Osmoregulation is different: osmoregulation controls water and solute balance.

q: In humans and other mammals, the core body temperature is monitored by a part of the brain called the thermoregulatory centre located in the _____.
e: In humans and other mammals, the core body temperature is monitored by a part of the brain called the thermoregulatory centre located in the hypothalamus. The hypothalamus is the brain centre that coordinates thermoregulation and much of homeostasis. Cerebrum is not hypothalamus.

q: When body temperature increases, arterioles leading to capillary loops in the dermis dilate in a process called _____.
e: When body temperature increases, arterioles leading to capillary loops in the dermis dilate in a process called vasodilation. Vasodilation widens skin arterioles so more heat can be lost. Vasoconstriction is not vasodilation.

q: When body temperature decreases, hairs are pulled upright by the contraction of hair _____ muscles to trap insulating air.
e: When body temperature decreases, hairs are pulled upright by the contraction of hair erector muscles to trap insulating air. Erector pili muscles lift hairs to trap an insulating layer of air. Hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys. Flexor is not erector.

q: Speeding up of body's metabolism and _____ are mechanisms that generate more heat when body temperature decreases.
e: Speeding up of body's metabolism and shivering are mechanisms that generate more heat when body temperature decreases. Shivering makes muscles release heat when the body is too cold. Vasodilation is different: vasodilation widens skin arterioles so more heat can be lost.

q: The liver stores excess glucose as _____ if the concentration in the blood gets too high.
e: The liver stores excess glucose as glycogen if the concentration in the blood gets too high. Glycogen is the branched storage polysaccharide of animals. Hormones keep blood glucose within a narrow range.

q: If the level of sugar in the blood falls, alpha cells of the Islet of Langerhans release a hormone called _____.
e: If the level of sugar in the blood falls, alpha cells of the Islet of Langerhans release a hormone called glucagon. Glucagon raises blood glucose by triggering glycogen breakdown in the liver. The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin and glucagon. Insulin is different: insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: If the concentration of blood sugar increases, insulin is released from _____ cells of the Islet of Langerhans.
e: If the concentration of blood sugar increases, insulin is released from beta cells of the Islet of Langerhans. The islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin and glucagon. Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar. Delta is not beta.

q: The human kidneys filter about _____ litres of blood per day and produce, on average, 1.5 litres of urine.
e: The human kidneys filter about 1,500 litres of blood per day and produce, on average, 1.5 litres of urine. Kidneys excrete urea and regulate water and ions. Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons. 15 is not 1,500.

q: Each kidney consists of two regions; the outer region, the cortex and the inner region the _____.
e: Each kidney consists of two regions; the outer region, the cortex and the inner region the medulla. The medulla oblongata contains centres that help control breathing rate. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine. Pelvis is not medulla.

q: The pyramids in the kidney lead to a funnel-like structure called the _____ which connects with the ureter.
e: The pyramids in the kidney lead to a funnel-like structure called the pelvis which connects with the ureter. The kidney filters blood, balances water and salts, and forms urine. The ureter carries urine from kidney to bladder. Bladder is different: the bladder stores urine until it is released.

q: A nephron consists of a glomerulus, a Bowman's capsule and a long renal _____.
e: A nephron consists of a glomerulus, a Bowman's capsule and a long renal tubule. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus. Nephrons are the kidney's filtering and urine-forming units. Artery is not tubule.

q: Ultrafiltration forces fluid from the blood through the walls of the capillaries and the Bowman's capsule due to high blood _____ in the arteriole.
e: Ultrafiltration forces fluid from the blood through the walls of the capillaries and the Bowman's capsule due to high blood pressure in the arteriole. Bowman's capsule collects filtrate from the glomerulus. Capillaries are thin-walled vessels where exchange with tissues happens. Sugar is not pressure.

q: Selective reabsorption occurs in the tubule; the longer the loop of Henle, the greater the reabsorption of _____.
e: Selective reabsorption occurs in the tubule; the longer the loop of Henle, the greater the reabsorption of water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Urea is not water.

q: 'Antidiuresis' means producing less urine, controlled by the _____ hormone (ADH).
e: 'Antidiuresis' means producing less urine, controlled by the Antidiuretic hormone (ADH). Urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons. ADH, antidiuretic hormone, makes the kidney reabsorb more water. Thyroxine is not Antidiuretic.

q: When the body loses too much water, ADH causes the collecting ducts to become more _____ to water.
e: When the body loses too much water, ADH causes the collecting ducts to become more permeable to water. ADH, antidiuretic hormone, makes the kidney reabsorb more water. Rigid is not permeable.

q: Fruit ripening is one of the examples of a _____ biological feedback loop in plants.
e: Fruit ripening is one of the examples of a positive biological feedback loop in plants. Negative is not positive.

q: A ripe mango gives off a gas called _____ ($C_2H_4$) through its skin which signals neighbours to ripen.
e: A ripe mango gives off a gas called ethylene (C2H4) through its skin which signals neighbours to ripen. Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills. Oxygen is different: oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration.

q: A baby suckling on the mother's nipple stimulates the pituitary gland to release prolactin and _____.
e: A baby suckling on the mother's nipple stimulates the pituitary gland to release prolactin and oxytocin. Oxytocin is a hypothalamic hormone involved in birth and milk ejection. Insulin is different: insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar.

q: Prolactin stimulates milk production, while oxytocin stimulates smooth muscles contraction allowing milk to _____.
e: Prolactin stimulates milk production, while oxytocin stimulates smooth muscles contraction allowing milk to eject. Oxytocin is a hypothalamic hormone involved in birth and milk ejection. Store is not eject.

q: Successful homeostasis and being able to maintain it in adverse conditions is one of the most important _____ advantages.
e: Successful homeostasis and being able to maintain it in adverse conditions is one of the most important evolutionary advantages. Homeostasis is keeping the internal environment within narrow limits. Structural is not evolutionary.
